_comment: Octail curated egg (plan §6.4). Based on games-steamcmd core_keeper/egg-core-keeper.json (pelican-eggs, MIT licence). Octail makes the install fail when SteamCMD didn't download the server, and adds the core-keeper tag, a reserved query port (game port + 1), the no_console_input flag (the server has no console commands), install sandbox defaults and resource hints. SteamCMD is retried up to 3 times: its first run on a fresh install often fails with "Missing configuration". The startup follows the game's own _launch.sh instead of upstream's xvfb-run line: Xvfb and the server are started directly, the stop (Ctrl+C = SIGINT, which tini hands to the whole process group) and SIGTERM are trapped and sent to the server as SIGTERM, and the server is waited for, so it saves and quits instead of being killed when the shell exits (upstream trapped only SIGTERM and signalled xvfb-run, not the server), and the container ends when the server does (upstream waited on the log tail). The console also prints GameInfo.txt (join info: Game ID, or IP, port and password with -port) once the server wrote it, and an optional Server Password (-password) keeps the direct-connect password from changing at every start. The start line "Started session" is what the server logs when it is ready ("Started session with info: …", also what escapingnetwork/core-keeper-dedicated watches for). The server needs real CPU: on one shared core it starves (Steam networking "waited for lock" assertions) and may never reach that line; give it 2 cores. SteamCMD exits 0 even when an install failed (Missing configuration), so its retry loop counts a run as done only on SteamCMD's "Success! App" line.
name: Core Keeper
author: karsten@fiedleronline.net
description:
Core Keeper is a survival sandbox game for single or multiplayers.

--- Drawn towards a mysterious relic, you are an explorer who awakens in an ancient cavern of creatures, resources and trinkets. Trapped deep underground will your survival skills be up to the task? Mine relics and resources to build your base, craft new equipment, survive, and power up the Core. ---
startup: export DISPLAY=:99; rm -f ./GameID.txt ./GameInfo.txt ./CoreKeeperServerLog.txt /tmp/.X99-lock; touch ./CoreKeeperServerLog.txt; Xvfb :99 -screen 0 {{DISPLAY_WIDTH}}x{{DISPLAY_HEIGHT}}x{{DISPLAY_DEPTH}} -ac -nolisten tcp -nolisten unix & XVFBPID=$!; ./CoreKeeperServer -batchmode -logfile CoreKeeperServerLog.txt -world {{WORLD_INDEX}} -worldname "{{WORLD_NAME}}" -worldseed {{WORLD_SEED}} $([[ "{{GAME_ID}}" != "" ]] && echo -n " -gameid {{GAME_ID}}") $([[ "{{SERVER_PASSWORD}}" != "" ]] && echo -n " -password {{SERVER_PASSWORD}}") -maxplayers {{MAX_PLAYERS}} -worldmode {{WORLD_MODE}} -port {{SERVER_PORT}} & CKPID=$!; tail --pid=${CKPID} -n +1 -f CoreKeeperServerLog.txt | grep --line-buffered -e '^\[userid:[0-9]*\] player' -e '^[^\[]' & (while kill -0 ${CKPID} 2>/dev/null && [ ! -s GameInfo.txt ]; do sleep 2; done; [ -s GameInfo.txt ] && echo "Join info (GameInfo.txt):" && cat GameInfo.txt) & trap "kill -TERM ${CKPID} 2>/dev/null; wait ${CKPID}; kill ${XVFBPID} 2>/dev/null" INT TERM; wait ${CKPID}; kill ${XVFBPID} 2>/dev/null

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# steamcmd Base Installation Script
#
# Server Files: /mnt/server
# Image to install with is 'ghcr.io/parkervcp/installers:debian'

##
#
# Variables
# STEAM_USER, STEAM_PASS, STEAM_AUTH - Steam user setup. If a user has 2fa enabled it will most likely fail due to timeout. Leave blank for anon install.
# WINDOWS_INSTALL - if it's a windows server you want to install set to 1
# SRCDS_APPID - steam app id found here - https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/Dedicated_Servers_List
# SRCDS_BETAID - beta branch of a steam app. Leave blank to install normal branch
# SRCDS_BETAPASS - password for a beta branch should one be required during private or closed testing phases.. Leave blank for no password.
# INSTALL_FLAGS - Any additional SteamCMD  flags to pass during install.. Keep in mind that steamcmd auto update process in the docker image might overwrite or ignore these when it performs update on server boot.
# AUTO_UPDATE - Adding this variable to the egg allows disabling or enabling automated updates on boot. Boolean value. 0 to disable and 1 to enable.
#
 ##

# Install packages. Default packages below are not required if using our existing install image thus speeding up the install process.
#apt -y update
#apt -y --no-install-recommends install curl lib32gcc-s1 ca-certificates

## just in case someone removed the defaults.
if [[ "${STEAM_USER}" == "" ]] || [[ "${STEAM_PASS}" == "" ]]; then
    echo -e "steam user is not set.\n"
    echo -e "Using anonymous user.\n"
    STEAM_USER=anonymous
    STEAM_PASS=""
    STEAM_AUTH=""
else
    echo -e "user set to ${STEAM_USER}"
fi

## download and install steamcmd
cd /tmp
mkdir -p /mnt/server/steamcmd
curl -sSL -o steamcmd.tar.gz https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/client/installer/steamcmd_linux.tar.gz
tar -xzvf steamcmd.tar.gz -C /mnt/server/steamcmd
mkdir -p /mnt/server/steamapps # Fix steamcmd disk write error when this folder is missing
cd /mnt/server/steamcmd

# SteamCMD fails otherwise for some reason, even running as root.
# This is changed at the end of the install process anyways.
chown -R root:root /mnt
export HOME=/mnt/server

## install game using steamcmd
## Octail: SteamCMD's first run often fails with "Missing configuration"; try up to 3 times
for steamcmd_try in 1 2 3; do
    if ./steamcmd.sh +force_install_dir /mnt/server +login ${STEAM_USER} ${STEAM_PASS} ${STEAM_AUTH} $( [[ "${WINDOWS_INSTALL}" == "1" ]] && printf %s '+@sSteamCmdForcePlatformType windows' ) +app_update ${SRCDS_APPID} validate +quit 2>&1 | tee /tmp/steamcmd.log && grep -q "Success! App '" /tmp/steamcmd.log && ! grep -q "ERROR! Failed to install app" /tmp/steamcmd.log; then break; fi
    echo "SteamCMD did not finish (attempt $steamcmd_try of 3)"
done

## set up 32 bit libraries
mkdir -p /mnt/server/.steam/sdk32
cp -v linux32/steamclient.so ../.steam/sdk32/steamclient.so

## set up 64 bit libraries
mkdir -p /mnt/server/.steam/sdk64
cp -v linux64/steamclient.so ../.steam/sdk64/steamclient.so

## add below your custom commands if needed

## Octail: fail the install when SteamCMD didn't download the server
if [[ ! -f "/mnt/server/CoreKeeperServer" ]]; then
    echo -e "\nSteamCMD failed to install the Core Keeper dedicated server; try reinstalling."
    exit 1
fi

## install end
echo "-----------------------------------------"
echo "Installation completed..."
echo "-----------------------------------------"

variables.name: World Index
variables.description: Which world index to use. Default: 0.

variables.name: World Name
variables.description: The name to use for the server. Defaul: Core Keeper Server.

variables.name: World Seed
variables.description: The seed to use for a new world. Set to 0 to generate random seed. Default: 0.

variables.name: Game ID
variables.description: Game ID to use for the server. Needs to be at least 28 characters and alphanumeric, excluding Y,y,x,0,O. Empty or not valid means a new ID will be generated at start. Default: EMPTY.

variables.name: Server Password
variables.description: Password for joining by IP (direct connection, which this server uses since it listens on its port). Up to 28 letters and digits. Empty: the server makes a new random one at every start (shown in the console and GameInfo.txt).

variables.name: Max Players
variables.description: Maximum number of players that will be allowed to connect to server. Maximum is 100. Default: 100,

variables.name: World Mode
variables.description: Whether to use normal (0) or hard (1) mode for world.

variables.name: Steam App ID
variables.description: Steam App ID of Core Keeper Dedicated Server

variables.name: Steam Query Port
variables.description: Core Keeper answers Steam queries on the game port + 1. Set by Octail when the server is created (the port after the game port). The game picks this port itself and doesn't read this setting; Octail only reserves it.
